items.title: Joined populate throws when embedded property has the same name as its column
items.body:
### Describe the bug

After upgrading from v6 to v7, populating a relation with the joined strategy started throwing for one of our entities.

The entity has an embeddable with a single property, and that property's column has the same name as the embedded property itself (`User.password` -> `Password.value` stored in the `password` column, `prefix: ''`). Loading `User` directly works, `select-in` works, only the joined populate fails:

```
DriverException: Cannot use 'as u1__password' alias on embedded property 'u1.password' because it expands to multiple columns. Alias individual fields instead (e.g. 'u1.password.propertyName as u1__password').
```

The error message was confusing to me since the embeddable only has one column and I'm not aliasing anything myself, the alias comes from the populate. My guess is `u1.password` gets resolved to the embedded property instead of the `password` column.

v6 had a problem with the same setup too, just a different one: the joined load works, but if you then change another entity and flush, it tries to update `user` with nothing in it:

```
Empty .update() call detected! Update data does not contain any values to update. This will result in a faulty query. Table: `user`. Columns: .
```

Again only after a joined load, select-in is fine.

Renaming the embedded property (we went with `hashedPassword`) makes both go away, so we're fine for now, but it took a while to figure out what was going on.

Might be related to #8271 / #8272, but it still fails on 7.2.1 and on the current `next`, which should already have that fix.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/JH8459/reproduction

`src/example.test.ts` has 4 tests. direct load and select-in pass, joined populate and the flush one fail.

- 7.2.1-dev.24 (next): joined populate + flush fail
- 7.2.1, 7.2.0: same
- 6.6.16: joined populate passes, flush fails with the empty update

I also tried it on mariadb 11.4, same results.

### What driver are you using?

@mikro-orm/sqlite (also reproduced with @mikro-orm/mariadb)

### MikroORM version

7.2.1-dev.24

### Node.js version

v24.11.0

### Operating system

macOS

items.title: Upgrade guide says em.transactional defaults to REQUIRES_NEW, Transactions page says NESTED
items.body:
Two docs pages disagree with each other on the default propagation for `em.transactional`, and I think one of them is just wrong.

Transactions page (`transactions.md#transaction-propagation`):

> By default, MikroORM uses `NESTED` propagation for explicit transactions via `em.transactional`. When you call `em.transactional()` within another transaction, it automatically creates a savepoint (nested transaction) rather than joining the existing transaction.

Upgrade guide (`upgrading-v6-to-v7.md`, "Default propagation in `@Transactional` is `REQUIRED`"):

> The previous default was `REQUIRES_NEW`, which always started a new transaction. `REQUIRES_NEW` remains the default for the `em.transactional` method.

Before opening a PR I went and checked which one matches reality. `em.transactional()` calls `TransactionManager.handle()`, which does `options.propagation ??= TransactionPropagation.NESTED` (`packages/core/src/utils/TransactionManager.ts:23`) — that's the only code path, there's no branch where it falls back to `REQUIRES_NEW`. The JSDoc on `EntityManager.transactional()` says the same thing in plain English ("a new savepoint (nested transaction) will be created by default"), and `tests/features/transactions/transaction-propagation.sqlite.test.ts` has a test specifically checking that nesting produces a `SAVEPOINT`. So the Transactions page is right and the upgrade guide sentence is wrong.

I also checked whether the upgrade guide used to be correct and just went stale. It didn't, as far as I can tell — the `options.propagation ??=` line hasn't changed since it was introduced in #6802, and it was already `NESTED` there. The wrong sentence got added later, in the same commit that changed the *decorator's* default to `REQUIRED`, but that commit didn't touch `em.transactional`'s default at all (only a type signature widening). So it looks like the sentence was wrong from the moment it was written, probably a mix-up between "the decorator used to default to REQUIRES_NEW" and "em.transactional still defaults to REQUIRES_NEW."

Same sentence shows up in both `docs/docs/upgrading-v6-to-v7.md` and the `version-7.2` snapshot, word for word.

Proposed fix, matching how the Transactions page already phrases it:

> `NESTED` remains the default for the `em.transactional` method, which creates a savepoint when a transaction is already active.

Happy to send a PR for this — just didn't want to guess which of your own two pages was the intended source of truth before submitting the diff.

items.title: Setting a nullable `array: true` embedded to `null` is silently dropped when passing an entity instance to `qb().update()`
[v6→v7 migration] Nested to-one populate returns empty scalar fields when mixed with to-many populate under default `balanced` strategy
Array `$contains` (`@>`) nested under a relation in `populateWhere` is serialized as a record tuple in the JOIN-ON condition
items.body:
### Describe the bug

After upgrading to v7, a **multi-element** array operator (`$contains` / `@>`) that lands inside a **JOIN-ON** predicate is serialized as a record tuple instead of an array literal. A condition lands in the JOIN-ON when it is **nested under a relation** — e.g. inside `populateWhere`, or a relation filter inside `where`.

Concretely, `{ scope: { $contains: ['DEAL', 'PROJECT'] } }` nested under a relation produces:

```sql
... inner join "tag" "t1" on "t0"."tag_id" = "t1"."id"
    and "t1"."scope" @> ('{DEAL,PROJECT}', undefined)
```

i.e. the array is collapsed into a 2-element **tuple** whose first element is the full array literal `'{DEAL,PROJECT}'` and whose second element is the literal `undefined`. Postgres then fails with:

```
column "undefined" does not exist
```

The **same filter placed in the flat top-level WHERE serializes correctly**:

```sql
... where "t0"."scope" @> '{DEAL,PROJECT}'   -- correct
```

A **single-element** array is harmless because `@> ('{DEAL}')` is equivalent to `@> '{DEAL}'`; the bug only manifests with **2+ elements**.

This is a regression from v6, where the array literal was produced in both positions.

> Note: depending on the exact column type / nesting, the malformed tuple can also surface as `operator does not exist: text[] @> record` (SQLSTATE 42883) instead of `column "undefined" does not exist`. Both stem from the same root cause: the array operand is rendered as a record/tuple in the JOIN-ON code path rather than as an array.

## Reproduction

Minimal runnable repro (entities + a 3-test vitest file) is here: **https://github.com/jison228/mikroorm-contains-joinon-repro**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/jison228/mikroorm-contains-joinon-repro
cd mikroorm-contains-joinon-repro && npm install
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@localhost:5432/your_db npm test
# -> middle test fails: column "undefined" does not exist
```

The essence:

```ts
@Entity()
class Tag {
  @PrimaryKey({ type: 'number' }) id!: number;

  @Enum({ items: () => Scope, array: true }) // also reproduces with @Property({ type: 'string[]' })
  scope!: Scope[];

  @OneToMany(() => Item, (i) => i.tag) items = new Collection<Item>(this);
}

@Entity()
class Item {
  @PrimaryKey({ type: 'number' }) id!: number;
  @ManyToOne(() => Tag) tag!: Tag;
}

// ✅ flat WHERE -> "scope" @> '{DEAL,PROJECT}'
await em.find(Tag, { scope: { $contains: ['DEAL', 'PROJECT'] } });

// ❌ same filter under a relation -> JOIN-ON -> "scope" @> ('{DEAL,PROJECT}', undefined)
await em.find(Item, {}, {
  populate: ['tag'],
  populateWhere: { tag: { scope: { $contains: ['DEAL', 'PROJECT'] } } },
});
```

Verified against PostgreSQL with both an `@Enum({ items, array: true })` column and a plain `@Property({ type: 'string[]' })` column — identical malformed JOIN-ON output in both cases.

## Expected behavior

The array operator should serialize identically whether the predicate lands in the flat WHERE or in a JOIN-ON condition — always as an array literal / single array-bound parameter (`"scope" @> '{DEAL,PROJECT}'`), never as a record tuple `("...", undefined)`.

## Additional context

- This looks like the same class of bug as a previously reported/fixed JOIN-ON array case, but reached via `populateWhere` on a relation; the array-vs-tuple handling does not appear to be applied in this JOIN-ON path.
- Single-element arrays mask the bug (`(?)` === `?`); reproduce with **2+** elements.

## Versions

| Dependency | Version |
| --- | --- |
| node | 20.19.5 |
| typescript | 5.6.3 |
| mikro-orm | 7.1.4 |
| @mikro-orm/postgresql | 7.1.4 |
| @mikro-orm/decorators | 7.1.4 |
| Database | PostgreSQL (Docker `postgres`) |

### Reproduction

https://github.com/jison228/mikroorm-contains-joinon-repro

### What driver are you using?

@mikro-orm/postgresql

### MikroORM version

7.1.4

### Node.js version

24.14.1

### Operating system

Alpine Linux 3.22 (node:24-alpine3.22)

items.title: Bun build fails after SQLite v7 upgrade due to unsupported better-sqlite3
items.body:
### Describe the bug

After upgrading to SQLite v7, the project fails to build when running with Bun. The error shown is:

`'better-sqlite3' is not yet supported in Bun.`

This appears to be caused by Bun’s lack of support for native modules like `better-sqlite3`, which gets reinstalled or rebuilt during the upgrade. The referenced PR is still an open issue and hasn’t been implemented in a stable Bun release yet.

items.title: duplicated entities when building with Bun (MikroORM v7 + better-auth)
items.body:
### Describe the bug

Hi,

I recently upgraded to MikroORM v7 and switched to the `defineEntity` + class pattern as recommended in the documentation. I'm using **Bun 1.3.10** along with **better-auth**.

### Problem

When I build my project using:

```bash
bun build --target bun --outfile server.js server.ts
```

I notice that all better-auth entities are duplicated during discovery:

```
[info] MikroORM version: 7.0.5
[discovery] ORM entity discovery started
[discovery] - processing entity Account
[discovery] - processing entity Account2
[discovery] - processing entity User
[discovery] - processing entity User2
[discovery] - processing entity Verification
[discovery] - processing entity Verification2
[discovery] - processing entity SpokenLanguage
[discovery] - processing entity Skill
[discovery] - processing entity Session
[discovery] - processing entity Session2
[discovery] - processing entity Message
[discovery] - processing entity FileStorage
[discovery] - processing entity EmbeddableTranslations
[discovery] - processing entity AdminOmnisearch
```

However, this issue does not occur when running the app directly with:

```
bun run server.ts
```

### Additional observation

I also noticed that when defining entities, the name property must match the class name.

For example:

```ts
const SessionSchema = defineEntity({
  name: "SessionTest",
  tableName: "sessions",
  properties: (p) => ({
    ...primaryKeyProperty,
    expiresAt: p.datetime().type("timestamptz"),
    token: p.text().unique(),
    createdAt: dateTimeWithTimezone.nullable(),
    updatedAt: dateTimeWithTimezone,
    ipAddress: p.string(),
    userAgent: p.string(),
    impersonatedBy: p.string().nullable(),
    user: () => p.manyToOne(User),
  }),
  indexes: [{ name: "sessions_user_id_index", properties: ["user"] }],
});

export class Session extends SessionSchema.class {}
SessionSchema.setClass(Session);
```

Running this with:

```
bun run server.ts
```

produces two entities during discovery:

```
[info] MikroORM version: 7.0.5
[discovery] ORM entity discovery started
[discovery] - processing entity SessionTest
[discovery] - processing entity Session
```

With MikroORM v6, I was using the defineEntity API without encountering this issue.

### Workaround

If I named the `Session` Entity something other than Session, it solved the problem.

### Reproduction

The aboved issue is difficult to reproduce because a whole all setup with better-auth is complicated. If needed, I can provide you an access to our private code base.

Clone https://github.com/alexandre-dos-reis/mikro-orm-duplicated-entities/tree/master

and run `bun run ./src/orm.ts`

### What driver are you using?

@mikro-orm/postgresql

### MikroORM version

7.0.5

### Node.js version

Bun 1.3.10

### Operating system

linux

items.title: No entities were discovered on folder-based discovery
items.body:
### Describe the bug

I recently upgraded my `@mikro-orm/*` packages from v6.5.7 to the latest version and followed the upgrade guidelines carefully. My project is using NestJS with SWC.

However, when starting the application, I encountered the following error:

After some investigation, it appears the issue may originate from the entity discovery logic in `discover-entities.ts`:
https://github.com/mikro-orm/mikro-orm/blob/134843c0e836a382857624ed80bd569330ccdc41/packages/core/src/metadata/discover-entities.ts#L15

Specifically, the logic used to determine a valid entity target:
https://github.com/mikro-orm/mikro-orm/blob/134843c0e836a382857624ed80bd569330ccdc41/packages/core/src/metadata/discover-entities.ts#L30

When using CommonJS output (e.g., from SWC), the imported module structure looks like this:
```typescript
{
  exports: [Module: null prototype] {
    __esModule: true,
    default: { Staff: [Getter] },
    'module.exports': { Staff: [Getter] }
  }
}
```

In this case, the actual entity (Staff) is nested under default, and the current `validTarget` check evaluates to false, causing the entity to be ignored during discovery.

It seems that the current implementation may not fully account for CommonJS module shapes when using dynamic `import()`, especially with SWC output.

### Reproduction

-

### What driver are you using?

@mikro-orm/postgresql

### MikroORM version

v7.0.3

### Node.js version

v24.14.0

### Operating system

MacOS 26.3.1
